hits.section: ### F7 — Cote 47, scan 8, first paragraph and unfinished verification
hits.text: **Editorial proof plan:** the direct image of the Poincaré line bundle is perfect, and the zero-section pushforward is perfect because that section is a regular immersion, so the cone of the proposed comparison is perfect. Vanishing of all its derived residue-field fibres then proves that the cone vanishes, by the local perfect-complex criterion (The Stacks Project Authors, 2026, Tags 0DJT and 0G99). The remaining task is to show that the particular map induces the required isomorphisms at the unit, not merely that the two sides have equal cohomology dimensions. **Confidence: high**, because the finite-complex criterion is established and isolates exactly the manuscript’s unfinished step.

hits.text: The displayed identity \(\Lambda_Y=\varphi^*\Lambda_X^2\varphi_*\) has degree \(-2\), since restriction has degree zero and the Gysin map raises degree by two, so it transports algebraicity downward when \(\Lambda_X\) is already algebraic. Reversing that argument in the source requires critical-degree algebraicity on a self-product or an adjacent hyperplane product; Kleiman (1968, §§2.12–2.14) proves the corresponding hyperplane and flag implications. Consequently the letter's \(A(k)=C(k)\) concerns conditions quantified over all relevant varieties, not an implication from the weak condition on a single \(X\) to its own strong condition. Grothendieck (1969, §3) likewise distinguishes \(B(X)\Rightarrow A(X)\) from \(A(X\times X)\Rightarrow B(X)\).

If the cycle-class map has the stated injectivity and \(\operatorname{NS}(X)\) has rank \(\rho\), this gives the dimension calculation \(\dim V_\ell\operatorname{Br}'(X)=b_2-\rho\). Neither calculation recovers finite \(\ell\)-primary groups, so the torsion comparisons elsewhere in (8.3)–(8.7) remain separate information rather than consequences of the dimension formula. This is a useful check on what “transcendental part” means in this particular passage.
